event_date_basis: developer.apple.com/news/?id=likeohx4 carries the visible article date line September 16, 2026; the announcement's own text states "Starting today, multiseat purchases are enabled by default for subscriptions in App Store Connect," which is the one change that takes effect on the announcement date itself. Two other dates on the same page are forward-looking and are kept separate in this article: Volume Purchasing launches 2026-10-22, and Group Purchases and Bundles/Suites are only dated "this winter" or "later this year" with no calendar date. A fourth, earlier date lives only in the ENGLISH App Store Connect help page: subscriptions created before 2026-09-14 that do not use StoreKit 2 or that have Family Sharing on are opted out by default -- that cutoff is two days before the announcement and is written in the article as a threshold, not as an event. The Traditional-Chinese version of that same help page does not carry the 2026-09-14 date at all (verified 2026-09-18 by substring search on both pages), so the article attributes the cutoff to the English version explicitly.
title: App Store 訂閱新規則：組合方案最多五個開發者、多名額購買預設開啟、大量採購 10 月 22 日上路

sources.title: Get your subscriptions ready for iOS 27
Create Bundles and Suites for auto-renewable subscriptions
Manage purchase options for an auto-renewable subscription
管理自動續訂型訂閱的購買選項
sources.publisher: Apple (App Store Connect 說明，繁體中文版)

sourcing_notes:
2026-09-18, independent factcheck re-fetch. All four sources fetched with curl -sL -A "Mokaair-editorial" (no email, name or personal data in any UA, header, query string or form) into the session scratchpad before any editing: (1) https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=likeohx4 -> HTTP 200, 117,728 bytes, article body present; (2) https://developer.apple.com/app-store/subscriptions/bundles-and-suites/ -> HTTP 200, 115,481 bytes, body present including the Q&A block; (3) https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-subscriptions/manage-purchase-options-for-auto-renewable-subscriptions -> HTTP 200, 370,868 bytes, body present; (4) https://developer.apple.com/tw/help/app-store-connect/manage-subscriptions/manage-purchase-options-for-auto-renewable-subscriptions -> HTTP 200, 370,996 bytes, fully translated body present. Byte counts for (1)-(3) are identical to the writing pass earlier the same day.

SOURCE-LIST CHANGE MADE BY THE FACTCHECK: source (4) is new. The writing pass and the prior research pass both recorded that "Apple has not published a Traditional-Chinese version" and that "/tw/ returns HTTP 404", generalising from the one /tw/ URL that was actually tried (the news item). Each /tw/ URL was tested separately: developer.apple.com/tw/news/?id=likeohx4 -> 404 (81,990-byte soft 404); developer.apple.com/tw/app-store/subscriptions/bundles-and-suites/ -> 404 (82,022 bytes); but the help page's /tw/ URL -> 200 with a complete Traditional-Chinese translation titled 〈管理自動續訂型訂閱的購買選項〉.

LOCALISATION, RE-TESTED IN FULL BY THE SECOND ROUND. The first factcheck tested only /tw/ and /cn/ and then wrote "the announcement is zh-CN only", which is a second over-generalisation of the same kind. Measured 2026-09-18: announcement /cn/ 200 (118,619 bytes), /jp/ 200 (126,192, headline 「iOS 27に向けたサブスクリプションの準備」), /kr/ 200 (124,432), /tw/ 404; Bundles page /tw/ 404, /cn/ 404 (83,051), /jp/ 404 (84,886); help page /tw/ 200 and /cn/ 200 (370,625). So the announcement is translated into several languages but not Traditional Chinese, the Bundles page is unlocalised in every language tested, and the help page exists in both Chinese scripts. The article's paragraph 2 states this per page and names only the languages actually tested.

TERMINOLOGY CONSEQUENCE: because the zh-TW help page exists, Apple's own Traditional-Chinese wording is available and BRIEF.md's rule (介面名稱對照各語言的官方說明頁，不要自己翻) applies. Apple's zh-TW page writes 多名額購買 (multiseat purchases), 名額 (seat), 群組購買者 (group purchaser), 自動續訂型訂閱 (auto-renewable subscription), 「Apple 商務」 (Apple Business), 「Apple 校務管理」 (Apple School Manager), 大量採購 (volume purchase), 以群組形式購買 (purchase as a group). The article previously used the invented 多人席次購買／席次／團體購買人／量購／團體購買; it has been changed to Apple's published zh-TW terms wherever Apple publishes one. Bundle and Suite have NO Chinese page of any kind (the zh-CN announcement even labels its link to the Bundles page 「(英文)」), so 組合方案 and 套組 remain this site's translations and are flagged as such in paragraph 2.

ONE MORE WORD IS THIS SITE'S, NOT APPLE'S -- corrected by the second round. 群組購買 (Group Purchases, as a product name) is NOT published in zh-TW: all five occurrences of that string on the zh-TW help page are inside 群組購買者 (group purchaser). What Apple publishes for the act is the verb phrase 以群組形式購買. 大量採購 IS published as a noun (「僅能在「Apple 商務」中大量採購」, twice). So the zh-TW words taken verbatim from Apple are 多名額購買, 名額, 群組購買者, 自動續訂型訂閱, 「Apple 商務」, 「Apple 校務管理」, 大量採購 and 以群組形式購買; 組合方案, 套組 and the product name 群組購買 are this site's, and the article prints the English original beside each of the three.

FOR THE zh-CN TRANSLATION, Apple is split between its own two pages and the translator must not merge them. The zh-CN announcement uses 套装 (Bundle), 套件 (Suite), 多席位购买, 席位, 批量购买, 群组购买, Apple 商务, Apple 校园教务管理. The zh-CN help page -- the same document as sources 3 and 4 -- uses 多名额购买, 名额, 群组购买者, 自动续期订阅, 批量购买, Apple 商务, Apple 校园教务管理, and contains 多席位购买 and 席位 zero times. Pick per page and say which page each word came from; do not reuse the zh-TW words in either case.

NON-BREAKING SPACES: every verbatim_quote below was tested as an exact substring against the saved page, not assumed. U+00A0 placement on developer.apple.com is inconsistent even within one page (the news item has 'Volume' + U+00A0 + 'Purchasing' in the launch-date sentence but an ordinary space in 'With Volume Purchasing, organizations...'), so pattern-matching the entity rather than testing the position produces quotes that cannot be found. Two quotes carried over from the writing pass failed that test today and were corrected: fact 3 had 'With' + U+00A0 + 'Suites' where the page has an ordinary space, and fact 11 had 'Volume' + U+00A0 + 'Purchasing' where that sentence has an ordinary space. 17 of the writing pass's 19 quotes passed unchanged; all 30 quotes in this record, including the 11 added by this check, were verified as exact substrings after the fix. The second round re-fetched all four pages (identical byte counts) and re-ran the same exact-substring test: 30/30 passed unchanged, and the 3 quotes it added bring the record to 33/33.

SOURCE'S OWN TYPO, reproduced rather than silently fixed: the English help page joins two sentences with a comma -- 'Existing customers' subscriptions continue to renew until the group purchaser cancels, New seats cannot be added, but can be removed by the group purchaser.' The capital N after the comma is Apple's, not ours.

Not opened this session: the two WWDC26 session videos linked from the news item, and the request-access form itself (behind a developer account login).

verified_facts.fact: The announcement's general advice to developers preparing for iOS 27 subscription changes: start by confirming apps use StoreKit 2 for Apple In-App Purchases.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: You can start preparing today by making sure your apps use StoreKit 2 to handle your Apple In-App Purchases.

verified_facts.fact: Bundle definition: multiple subscriptions accessible in one purchase, spanning a single app, multiple apps from the same developer, or even multiple different developers' apps.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: With Bundles, people can access multiple subscriptions in one purchase — across a single app, multiple apps from the same developer, or even spanning multiple developers’ apps.

verified_facts.fact: Suite definition, distinct from Bundle: a single subscription that works across a set of apps from one developer, not multiple subscriptions combined. Note this is a definition, not a stated prohibition -- Apple nowhere says a Suite may not span developers, so the article says 官方定義為同一開發者 rather than 僅限單一開發者.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: With Suites, people get access to a single subscription that seamlessly works across a set of apps from a single developer.

verified_facts.fact: The hard ceiling on a multi-developer Bundle: up to five developers.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Up to five developers can participate in a multi-developer Bundle.

verified_facts.fact: Two further numeric caps, stated only in the Bundles page Q&A and missed by both earlier passes: a Bundle may contain up to 5 subscriptions, and a Suite may span up to 15 apps. These are different quantities from the five-developer ceiling and the article now states both so the two fives are not conflated.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: You can include up to 5 subscriptions in a Bundle. A Suite can provide a subscription across up to 15 apps.

verified_facts.fact: Apple's own illustrations (not observed products): a single-developer Bundle example is a music-streaming subscription plus a podcast subscription sold together at a lower price than subscribing separately; a multi-developer Bundle example is a fitness-tracking app and a nutrition-planning app from two different developers partnering on a health-and-wellness Bundle.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Single developer Bundle: People can purchase multiple auto-renewable subscriptions from the same Apple Developer account as a Bundle, at a lower price than subscribing to each individually.

verified_facts.fact: A subscriber can modify a Bundle purchase at any time through their Apple Account, choosing to keep individual services or cancel the whole Bundle. The partial-keep option is stated for Bundles only.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: If someone needs to modify their Bundle purchase, they can do so at any time through their Apple Account, where they can choose to stay subscribed to individual services or cancel the entire Bundle.

verified_facts.fact: When those changes take effect -- the qualifier the writing pass dropped. Cancelling a Bundle or Suite is possible at any time, but cancellations and partial changes land at the next renewal date; only upgrades are immediate.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Any cancellations or partial changes will take effect at the next renewal date. Upgrades take effect immediately, giving subscribers instant access to their additional content at the time of purchase.

verified_facts.fact: What happens to an existing standalone subscriber who buys a Bundle containing it: immediate upgrade plus a prorated refund for the remainder of the standalone period. Both earlier research passes listed this under not_said as something Apple never addresses; the Bundles page Q&A answers it directly.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: If someone purchases a Bundle that includes a subscription they’ve already purchased, they’ll be upgraded and immediately get access to all subscriptions it includes. They’ll also receive a prorated refund for the remainder of their standalone subscription period.

verified_facts.fact: Requirement that every subscription in a Bundle share the same duration -- a monthly and an annual subscription cannot be combined.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Offer the same subscription duration for each auto-renewable subscription included in a Bundle.

verified_facts.fact: Availability of Bundles and Suites is a vague period plus a version floor, no date: later this year on iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, tvOS 27 or later. Access is also gated behind a request form; the page's own section heading for that gate is 'Request access and submit for review'. That heading string is present in bundles-and-suites and absent from the news item -- searched on both pages today, confirming the writing pass's re-attribution away from the news URL.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Request access and submit for review

verified_facts.fact: Extra conditions on a multi-developer Bundle, from the same section: every participating developer files its own interest form and signs a named legal addendum before configuration starts; and Bundles and Suites are configured and published in batches.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Each participating developer will need to sign the Multi-Developer Bundle Program Legal Addendum and provide Apple with their subscription details through an intake form before configuration can begin.

verified_facts.fact: Pricing is settled privately per Bundle during configuration, which is also where each Bundle's go-live date is set. Apple publishes no prices and no commission terms anywhere in these pages.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: This includes gathering details about your subscription, as well as confirming your pricing and go-live date.

verified_facts.fact: Same availability sentence appears (independently) on the news item, phrased as a direct statement about Bundles and Suites.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Bundles and Suites will be available later this year in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, tvOS 27, or later.

verified_facts.fact: Multiseat purchasing took effect on the announcement day itself: enabled by default for subscriptions in App Store Connect starting that day, with full developer control to disable it entirely or manage availability per store.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Starting today, multiseat purchases are enabled by default for subscriptions in App Store Connect.

verified_facts.fact: Volume Purchasing mechanics: organizations using Apple Business and Apple School Manager buy through a single Apple In-App Purchase and assign seats using a device management provider.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: With Volume Purchasing, organizations that use Apple Business and Apple School Manager can buy your subscriptions through a single Apple In-App Purchase and assign seats using a device management provider.

verified_facts.fact: Group Purchases mechanics: a subscriber buys multiple seats in one Apple In-App Purchase and invites others to join, with Apple handling seat assignment and invitations.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: With Group Purchases, a subscriber can buy multiple seats in a single Apple In-App Purchase and invite others to join.

verified_facts.fact: The one calendar date in the announcement's body, next to an undated one: Volume Purchasing launches October 22, 2026; Group Purchases will launch 'this winter' with no hemisphere or exact date given. (The page's own dateline, September 16, 2026, is a date too, so the article says 公告正文只寫出一個明確的未來日期 rather than calling 10-22 the only date on the page.)
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Volume Purchasing launches on October 22, 2026, and Group Purchases will launch this winter.

verified_facts.fact: Definition of multiseat purchasing and the group purchaser role: a customer can buy a subscription in quantities greater than 1; that customer, called the group purchaser, manages the shared subscription and controls access, letting a team, classroom or organization share access under one purchase.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Multiseat purchases allow a customer to buy a subscription in quantities greater than 1. This customer, known as the group purchaser, manages the shared subscription and controls who has access, making it possible for a team, classroom, or organization to share access under a single purchase.

verified_facts.fact: Store split: on the App Store, customers can buy individually or as a group; inside Apple Business and Apple School Manager, only the multiseat purchase mode is supported. These three are sales channels, not regions -- the article says so explicitly so the 'no region is named' point does not read as contradicting them.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: In Apple Business and Apple School Manager, only multiseat purchases are supported.

verified_facts.fact: The default-on rule applies to all auto-renewable subscriptions, not just new ones, with one dated exception whose two conditions are joined by OR, not AND: a subscription created before September 14, 2026 is opted out by default if it does not use StoreKit 2, or if it has Family Sharing turned on -- either one is enough. The article now spells this out because the Chinese 沒有使用 StoreKit 2 或開啟家人共享 can be misread as negating both.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Multiseat purchases are turned on by default for all auto-renewable subscriptions. Subscriptions created prior to September 14, 2026 that do not use StoreKit 2 or that have Family Sharing turned on are set to opted out by default.

verified_facts.fact: The same English page restates the opt-out rule a second time WITHOUT any date, and adds the reverse move the article now mentions: an opted-out subscription can be switched on at any time.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Default settings for existing subscriptions: Subscriptions are set to opted out by default if the app doesn't use StoreKit 2 or has Family Sharing turned on. If you want to offer multiseat purchases, you can turn them on at any time in App Store Connect.

verified_facts.fact: A carve-out neither earlier pass recorded, and a real limit on the article's 'developers can just turn it off' sentence: custom apps cannot manage purchase options at all and may not opt out of multiseat.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Managing purchase options is not available for subscriptions in custom apps. Subscriptions for custom apps will automatically be available on Apple Business, and Apple School Manager and you may not opt out of multiseat purchases.

verified_facts.fact: The help page's own, looser availability sentence for multiseat gives no dates at all, unlike the news item's routes: available for Business and Education organizations, and for App Store customers, later this year.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Multiseat purchases will be available for Business and Education organizations, and for App Store customers later this year.

verified_facts.fact: Advice to a developer who wants multiseat off: turn it off in App Store Connect, and the stated reason is to avoid impact to customers.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: If you don't want to allow multiseat purchasing for your subscription, edit your purchase options in App Store Connect to avoid any impact to customers.

verified_facts.fact: Consequences of disabling multiseat after approval: new customers cannot buy multiple seats and the subscription is removed from Apple Business and Apple School Manager; existing customers keep renewing until the group purchaser cancels; new seats cannot be added, but the group purchaser can remove seats. Quoted with Apple's own comma splice before 'New'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Existing customers' subscriptions continue to renew until the group purchaser cancels, New seats cannot be added, but can be removed by the group purchaser.

verified_facts.fact: English page on Family Sharing plus multiseat: the two CAN both be on, and the consequence is that only the group purchaser's access includes Family Sharing. Turning Family Sharing on is irreversible.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: If you've enabled multiseat purchases for a subscription, only the group purchaser's access will include Family Sharing. Once you turn on Family Sharing, you won't be able to turn it off.

verified_facts.fact: The English page's second and more explicit coexistence sentence, added by the second-round check because the article's section 4 quotes its 'when both ... are turned on' clause and the 其餘名額僅供個人使用 half, which the note above does not cover. Apple presents coexistence as a state the developer confirms, not one it forbids.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: only the group purchaser will be able to share with family members when both multiseat purchases and Family Sharing are turned on. All other seats will be for individual use only

verified_facts.fact: The Traditional-Chinese page ALSO states coexistence -- it translates both English sentences faithfully -- so the contradiction is not a clean English-vs-Chinese split. This is the zh-TW rendering, which opens the extra section and matches the English page, one sentence before the same section reverses itself. Note Apple uses 群組組織者 here and 群組購買者 five times elsewhere on the same page; the article follows the majority term.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: 若訂閱項目已開啟多名額購買功能，只有群組組織者具備使用「家人共享」的資格，所購買的其餘份數僅供個人使用。

verified_facts.fact: The reversal itself. The Traditional-Chinese page carries a section headed 「家人共享」和多名額購買 that the English page does not have ('Family Sharing and multiseat' appears 0 times in the English page, checked 2026-09-18), and its last two sentences say the opposite of everything above: enabling Family Sharing auto-disables multiseat, and the two cannot be enabled together. '9 月 14 日' appears 0 times in the Chinese page. The article reports the divergence, quotes the 無法...同時啟用 clause, and says it follows the English version without ruling either version wrong.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: 當你為已啟用多名額購買的訂閱項目開啟「家人共享」，系統會自動關閉其多名額購買功能。你可以隨時重新開啟多名額購買功能，但「家人共享」無法與多名額購買同時啟用。

verified_facts.fact: A consequence stated only on the Traditional-Chinese page and deliberately left out of the article for length: Apple says it WILL auto-disable multiseat on every existing auto-renewable subscription that has Family Sharing on. Future tense (會), not 已 -- do not write it as already done.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: 所有開啟「家人共享」的現有自動續訂型訂閱項目，Apple 會自動關閉其多名額購買功能。

verified_facts.fact: Apple's published Traditional-Chinese wording for the feature and the role, which the article now follows instead of inventing its own: 多名額購買 for multiseat purchases, 群組購買者 for group purchaser, 自動續訂型訂閱 for auto-renewable subscription.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: 多名額購買允許客戶一次購買不止一份的訂閱項目。這名客戶（即群組購買者）負責管理共享的訂閱項目並控管其存取權限，讓團隊、課堂或機構僅需一次購買就能共享存取權限。

verified_facts.fact: Apple's published Traditional-Chinese names for the two organisation stores and for buying in volume or as a group: 「Apple 商務」, 「Apple 校務管理」, 大量採購, 以群組形式購買.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: 在 App Store 中，客戶可選擇個別購買訂閱項目，或以群組形式購買；「Apple 商務」和「Apple 校務管理」則僅支援多名額購買。

not_said: No country or region is named anywhere in the bodies of the four pages for Bundles, Suites, Volume Purchasing or Group Purchases, and Taiwan is not mentioned. Write 官方未說明地區範圍, never 台灣可用 or 台灣不可用. Scope this to countries and regions only: the pages DO name three sales channels (App Store, Apple Business, Apple School Manager) and the help page's 'which stores can sell it' control refers to those three, not to regional storefronts. The article says so explicitly rather than claiming no storefront is mentioned at all.

No prices, no fee percentages, no commission or revenue split for a multi-developer Bundle. None of the pages says how revenue is divided among up to five developers, or whether the standard App Store commission changes. Apple says only that pricing is confirmed with the developer during configuration and that each participating developer signs the Multi-Developer Bundle Program Legal Addendum; the addendum's contents are not published.

No release date for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 or tvOS 27 themselves -- 'later this year' and 'this winter' are the only timing words besides the single 2026-10-22 date, plus the per-Bundle go-live date that Apple settles privately.

No minimum or maximum seat count for a group purchase -- only 'quantities greater than 1' on the help page. (This is separate from the Bundle/Suite caps of 5 subscriptions and 15 apps, which ARE published.)
Nothing on what happens if a participating developer withdraws from a multi-developer Bundle, or how disputes between bundled developers are handled.

CORRECTED TWICE -- read this whole entry before touching section 4's last paragraph. (1) Both pre-factcheck passes wrote that Apple never says whether Family Sharing and multiseat can coexist; Apple says so repeatedly. (2) The first factcheck then framed it as English-says-X, Chinese-says-Y, which is also wrong. The second round's per-sentence reading: the English page states coexistence twice and never denies it; the Traditional-Chinese page translates BOTH of those sentences faithfully AND adds a section the English page has no counterpart for, whose last two sentences deny coexistence. So the zh-TW page contradicts itself inside one paragraph, and the divergence is between that added section and everything else. Write it that way. Do not write 'the two language versions say the opposite', do not write a flat 'the two cannot coexist' or 'Apple does not say', and do not rule either version wrong -- the article may only state that it follows the English version and why.
No figures on uptake, adoption or how many developers are expected to use any of this.

No description of the consumer-side purchase screen, price display or App Store UI for a Bundle or Suite. The news item does say the App Store 'displays all apps included in your Bundle or Suite,' but describing that further would cross into UI description this site has not tested, so it is not used.

CORRECTED -- the earlier entry here was wrong. Both previous passes wrote that no page says whether an existing standalone subscriber can convert into a Bundle or what happens to the remaining paid period. The Bundles page Q&A answers exactly that: immediate upgrade plus a prorated refund for the remainder of the standalone period. Conversion into a Suite, or into a seat, is still not addressed.

CORRECTED TWICE. Both pre-factcheck passes wrote that Apple has published no Traditional-Chinese version at all; the first factcheck fixed that but then wrote that the announcement is 'zh-CN only'. Full per-URL testing on 2026-09-18 (second round): the App Store Connect help page has a complete zh-TW version (200) and a zh-CN version (200); the announcement returns 200 in zh-CN, Japanese and Korean and 404 in zh-TW; the Bundles and Suites page returns 404 in zh-TW, zh-CN and Japanese alike. So only the Bundles page is genuinely unlocalised, and the announcement is translated into several languages but not Traditional Chinese. Bundle and Suite therefore have no Chinese page of any kind, and 組合方案 and 套組 remain this site's translations; everything Apple does publish in zh-TW is used verbatim. Never state a language the check did not test.

unverified_or_excluded.claim: Content of the two WWDC26 session videos linked from the news item (Bundles and Suites video; a second video timestamped at 530 seconds).
unverified_or_excluded.why_excluded: Not opened in either session. No transcript was fetched, so nothing may be attributed to them.

unverified_or_excluded.claim: The full eligibility and configuration fields behind the 'Request access and submit for review' form on the Bundles and Suites page.
unverified_or_excluded.seen_where: developer.apple.com/app-store/subscriptions/bundles-and-suites/ -- the heading and the surrounding prose were read, the form itself sits behind a developer account login.
unverified_or_excluded.why_excluded: Never opened; do not describe form fields nobody here has seen.

unverified_or_excluded.claim: How revenue is split in a multi-developer Bundle, and whether Apple's commission changes for bundled purchases.
unverified_or_excluded.seen_where: Nowhere in the four sources; the Multi-Developer Bundle Program Legal Addendum is named but not published.
unverified_or_excluded.why_excluded: Apple does not say. The honest answer is 官方未說明, which is what the article uses.

unverified_or_excluded.claim: That multiseat purchasing responds to a specific competitor's feature or to regulatory pressure (e.g. the same week's EU app-store announcements).
unverified_or_excluded.seen_where: Not stated anywhere in the four sources; a tempting frame given other stories in this batch.
unverified_or_excluded.why_excluded: Apple gives only a market rationale (letting a team subscribe without IT or procurement). Supplying a motive would be invention.

unverified_or_excluded.claim: The Simplified-Chinese version of the same App Store Connect help page, read by the second round purely to test the Family Sharing divergence. It is a third version of the document and it settles nothing in the article's favour by itself, but it is the reason this check is confident the zh-TW section is the outlier: the zh-CN page carries the SAME extra 「家人共享」和多名额购买 section and the same auto-disable sentence, yet its third sentence reads 「你可以随时开启多名额购买，但『家人共享』不适用于多名额购买的其他名额」 -- other seats, not a ban on coexistence -- which agrees with the English page, while the zh-TW page's third sentence says the two 無法...同時啟用. The zh-CN page also omits the September 14, 2026 date, and its 現有訂閱預設值 sentence flips the condition to 未开启「家人共享」, the opposite of the English and zh-TW wording.
unverified_or_excluded.why_excluded: Not in sources[] and deliberately not added: the spec bars using a new URL to supply a fact, the article is already at the 4-source ceiling, and the article's stated reason for following the English version rests only on sources[] (the English page has no such section; inside the zh-TW page the contradiction is confined to one clause). editorial_brief: 讀者是在台灣使用或開發 App 的一般讀者。角度是：這篇公告同時鬆動 App Store 購買模式的兩個假設——組合方案／套組鬆動「一次購買只對應一個訂閱」，多名額購買鬆動「一次購買只給一個人用」。結構對應文章五節：(1) 公告談了什麼、哪一項當天生效；(2) 組合方案與套組的差別與條件，表格收尾；(3) 多名額購買的兩條路（大量採購與群組購買），圖解收尾；(4) 預設值變了——9 月 14 日這個分界，含自訂 App 的例外、Apple 給不想要此功能的開發者的建議與關閉後果，以及英文版與繁中版在家人共享上的不一致；(5) 官方沒有寫的事——地區、價格、分潤、席次上限，收尾放編輯設計的四人情境與『怎麼自己查』。全文刻意不談 Bundles 頁上的保留訊息 API（Retention Messaging API）——那是取消流程的功能，離本文的合購／多人購買主題較遠；它在 Bundles 頁，不在公告裡。用詞一律照 Apple 自己的繁體中文說明頁（多名額購買、名額、群組購買者、Apple 商務、Apple 校務管理、大量採購），只有 Bundle 與 Suite 沒有任何中文官方頁，才用本站翻譯的組合方案與套組並附英文原詞。
must_not_write: 不可以寫台灣可用或不可用；四頁正文都沒有寫出國家或地區，也沒有提到台灣，一律寫官方未說明地區範圍。但要把 App Store／Apple 商務／Apple 校務管理講成銷售管道，不要說成『連商店都沒提到』——頁面上有這三個管道。
不可以把 iOS 27、iPadOS 27、macOS 27、tvOS 27 換算成實際日期；官方唯一給的確定未來日期是 2026 年 10 月 22 日的大量採購。
不可以把 this winter 寫成某個月份，引用時要保留是 Apple 原文用詞、且未說明是哪個半球或哪一年。
不可以編造多開發者組合方案的分潤規則或抽成比例；官方只寫要簽 Multi-Developer Bundle Program Legal Addendum，附約內容未公開。
不可以把 2026 年 9 月 14 日的兩個條件寫成要同時成立；原文是 or，未使用 StoreKit 2、或開啟家人共享，符合其中一個就預設關閉。也不可以把這個日期寫成某件事發生的日子。
不可以在家人共享與多名額購買能否並存這件事上選邊，也不可以寫成『英文版與繁中版說法相反』：英文版兩次寫可以並存、從未否認，繁中版把那兩句都譯進去了，卻另外多出一節說不能並存——矛盾在繁中多寫的那一節與其餘內容之間。要寫出兩邊的句子並註明出處，只能說明本文以英文版為準的理由。
不可以再寫『Apple 沒有發布繁體中文版』，也不可以寫『公告只有簡體中文版』：App Store Connect 說明頁有完整繁中版與簡中版（都回 200），公告的簡中、日文、韓文版都回 200、繁中網址回 404，Bundles 頁的繁中、簡中、日文網址則全部回 404。沒實測過的語言不要寫。
不可以自創 Apple 已經發布過的中文介面名；多名額購買、名額、群組購買者、自動續訂型訂閱、Apple 商務、Apple 校務管理、大量採購一律照繁中說明頁。只有 Bundle 與 Suite 沒有中文官方頁，才用本站翻譯並附英文原詞。zh-CN 譯文另有 Apple 自己的簡體用詞（套装、套件、多席位购买、席位、批量购买、群组购买），不可以把繁中詞直接搬過去。
不可以寫『開發者不想要就能關掉』而不提例外；自訂 App 無法管理購買選項，也不能停用多名額購買。
不可以把組合方案的「最多五個開發者」與「最多五個訂閱」混為一談，套組另有「最多十五個 App」。
不可以描述使用者端的購買畫面或價格顯示；四頁都沒有截圖，本站也沒有實測。
不可以引用兩支 WWDC26 影片的內容，本次查核沒有開啟。
不寫划不划算、該不該訂——tech.md 禁止購買建議；整理條件差異可以，下結論不行。
不寫投資免責 callout——tech.md 規定科技垂直不帶。
主圖與 SVG 圖解不得出現商標、字標、圖示或介面截圖，產品名稱用純文字。
不要列表、不要 Markdown、不要 emoji，zh-TW 包不得出現簡體字。
